name: algol68g
why: A working Algol 68 interpreter opens a door into a historical language with a strange, almost alien syntax.

brief.what_it_is: Algol 68 Genie (a68g) is a free, GPL-licensed interpreter for Algol 68, a historical programming language. You give it Algol 68 source code and it runs the program, with runtime checks and a GDB-style debugger available during execution. It also offers arbitrary-precision integer, real and complex arithmetic. On Linux or FreeBSD it can optionally partially precompile well-debugged code to object code that is dynamically linked at runtime. The project describes itself as essentially feature-complete and ships with a Revised Report, a programming guide and example programs.
brief.why_it_exists: The project's stated aim is to preserve Algol 68 for educational and scientific-historical reasons, by providing a recent implementation written from scratch along with extensive documentation. The author wants people to be able to study the language and its context-dependent two-level grammar, and also use it for medium-sized programming tasks.
brief.how_it_works: It is an interpreter, like Python, that checks for uninitialised objects, out-of-range subscripts or values, dangling references and similar problems as the program runs. Its one extension to the language is Charles Lindsey's 1976 partial parametrization proposal, which gives the imperative language a functional sub-language. On Linux and FreeBSD, the optional precompilation step produces object code that the interpreter links in at runtime.
brief.install_notes: Downloads on the homepage are a source tarball (algol68g-3.13.4.tar.gz, 690 kB) for Linux or BSD, and a source archive with a WIN64 binary (algol68g-3.13.4.win64.zip, 2.2 MB) for Windows 11. The Windows binary is linked against the GNU Scientific Library, GNU plotutils and R mathlib, and the page says to run it from a command-line shell such as PowerShell. Precompiled binaries for major distributions are linked from a separate page. Detailed installation instructions are in the documentation, which I did not open. The brew formula name is algol68g and the executable is a68g.
brief.standout: It is one of the most complete Algol 68 implementations, and it was written from scratch rather than derived from an older compiler. Its hand-coded parser for the W-grammar is the basis of ga68, the Algol 68 front-end that was merged into GCC 16.1 as experimental, according to the homepage.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists version 3.13.4 with a date of 15 October 2026, the copyright line reads 2001-2026, and the page says recent releases mainly concern maintenance and additions to the runtime library. A post dated May 2026 covers GCC's Algol 68 support. Version 3 revisions have been released since 2022.
brief.caveats: The page says the project is not intended to modernise Algol 68; it aims to preserve the original language. The optional precompilation is available only on Linux and FreeBSD. Version 3 is developed on Debian and tested on FreeBSD and Windows 11. The Windows binary is run from a command-line shell rather than from a GUI. The homepage does not state the Windows binary's dependency details beyond the libraries named above. Many of the homepage's listed links, including the documentation PDF, the browsable source and the GitHub or SourceForge mirrors, were not followed.
quotes: It is an interpreter like Python, offering many runtime-checks and a GDB-style debugger.
The interpreter implements one extension to the language – Charles Lindsey's partial parametrization proposal published in 1976, that gives the imperative language Algol 68 a functional sub-language.
Note that responsibility for Algol 68 still lies with IFIP Working Group 2.1, and that it is not the intention of this project to modernise the language.
